brief: GS's TMT Today wrap reports a busy earnings morning. Micron beat on revenue ($54.23bn), EPS ($33.42) and DRAM/NAND revenue, with FY1Q guidance above Street on revenue and EPS but below on gross margin (86.25% vs Street 87.4%); the stock still traded -1% in premarket. Micron also raised its strategic customer agreement count to 26 (from 16), covering about 35% of anticipated FY30 revenue with about $150bn in five-year committed revenue at floor prices. Accenture beat broadly (revenue, bookings, margin, EPS) against tempered expectations and guided FY27 revenue above Street; GS calls the resulting +17% premarket move potentially the largest one-day gain in company history, lifting CTSH and IBM in sympathy. Alphabet rose 2% after unveiling Gemini 4 Argon post-close, following a prior-day selloff on reports of internal skepticism about model performance; Google says Argon sets records on coding, cybersecurity and professional benchmarks and will roll out in phases to trusted partners pending a US government safety review. Synopsys held its roughly 5% Investor Day gain on raised long-term targets. Macro: the 10-year yield hit its highest level since 2002 (5.313%), oil and gold ticked higher, and France's new fiscal plan sent the OAT-Bund spread to its widest since 2012 before retracing.
